question.problem:
Let $R = [2,4] \times [0,1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 2x - y.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\},\,{P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Write down the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$
question.worked_solution:
The upper Riemann sum is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{M}_{ij}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

where $M_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$ 

We consider an arbitrary subregion $R_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$ over the $x$-axis and $y_{i-1}$ and $y_i$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/88ffe30ae5401e00502b35d851b216768aad69bf94236561617adf23e1ce058f.png)

Notice that

- $f(x,y) = 2x - y$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y) = 2x - y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/01b291ca7cd81b88cf6ed06fdcdb2ffcbb1f78255d0f57d496823d347c2fb0b3.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248837/assets/de36b521dea1f925754a9c630c3d4a2c405c087a191138f1eaaa5771becb8c21.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{ij} & =f({x}_{i},{y}_{j-1})=2{x}_{i}-{y}_{j-1}\end{aligned}
$$

for all $1\leq i\leq m$ and $1\leq j\leq n.$

Finally, the upper Riemann sum is 

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(2{x}_{i}-{y}_{j-1})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$
